As someone who owned my own dog shop and grooming service, I can say that what they did was completely unacceptable.

My best friend took her Pomeranian in just for a bath. She never authorized a haircut. However, when she picked him up, she discovered that they had cut his hair without her consent.

A professional groomer should be familiar with the characteristics of each breed. Pomeranians can have issues with coat growth and are a breed whose hair should not be cut unnecessarily. She was actually letting her coat grow out, and yet they decided to cut it without permission.

The most serious issue is that a professional should never perform a procedure that the owner hasn't requested. You don't know the dog's medical history or the consequences that a haircut can have on its health or coat.

This demonstrates a lack of knowledge and respect for the client's instructions. That's why I'm leaving this review, and I'm also going to report what happened. I hope no one else has to go through an experience like this.

I won't leave a bad review, because I still love this place and this is the first time this has happened, but I'm writing as a warning.

I've been taking my dog ​​to this groomer for almost a year, and she's always come out looking great. For the last few months, Pedro has been grooming her, and the results have always been good. This time, due to lack of time, I booked with the first available groomer, thinking they would all be equally skilled, but the result was completely different. Her paws were disproportionate, with strands of varying lengths, and the overall finish was sloppy.

The next day, I went to respectfully express my dissatisfaction. However, what disappointed me was the groomer's response. Instead of acknowledging that the work could have been better and saying she would try to improve it, she became defensive and justified it by saying that if I touched her fur, some hairs would obviously be longer than others, and that my dog ​​couldn't be groomed the way I expected because of her coat type. Even after I showed her photos of how well they did the same job at the same place, she still just tried to justify the result.

She finally corrected the cut a little, but the way she handled the situation left much to be desired. What I expected was a bit of self-criticism to acknowledge the mistake. As a customer, you expect good service because that's what you're paying for, but I reiterate, before that, everything was excellent.

I've attached photos of how my dog ​​usually looked and how she looked this time (even after the correction).

My experience at Woofgang Groomers in Doral was completely disappointing.

I took my Yorkie to be groomed expecting him to be clean and well-cared for. When they returned him, he had the exact same eye discharge and food residue on his whiskers. They literally returned him with the same grime on his face. Is that what grooming is for?

The worst part wasn't just the poor work, but the way they treated me. When I complained respectfully, instead of offering a solution or at least checking the dog, they responded rudely and even threatened to call the police. Unbelievable.

Furthermore, one of the employees had the nerve to say that "the dog has eye discharge because he's old." My dog ​​isn't old; he's eight years old. And even if he were, that doesn't excuse returning a dog without cleaning his eyes and whiskers after a paid service.

The worst part is that this had already happened to me two years ago at the same place. At that moment, I decided not to return, but over time I forgot why. Today I remembered when they handed it back to me exactly as it had been the last time.

Grooming isn't just about cutting hair; it's about care, attention to detail, and friendly service. I found none of those three here.

I don't recommend it.

I’m not usually one to leave negative reviews, but I felt it was important to share my recent experience…especially for Dachshund owners considering this groomer.

I brought my Dachshund in for a mini groom, and when I picked him up, I was shocked to see that his beautiful, feathery tail had been cut extremely short—almost all the way to the base. When I asked the groomer about it, the response was: “I didn’t want to disturb the dog.” “The dog seemed to not want to be touched..”

In my view, if a groomer is unable to safely or confidently trim a specific area, I would much prefer they leave it untouched and inform me afterward, rather than making such a drastic cut.

I was genuinely upset by how his tail was cut and how the entire situation was handled. While I was offered an apology, I feel that, given the severity of the mistake, a refund or some form of compensation would have been more appropriate.

Sadly, I won’t be returning. I hope this helps other Dachshund owners. (SEE BEFORE & AFTER PHOTOS)

If you're looking for a place where they'll try to explain the inexplicable to you multiple times, just to charge over $200 for a haircut on a medium-sized dog... well, this is the place! There's no better one!

I recently watched the congressional hearing with airline CEOs when they were also trying to "explain" how irresponsible it is to charge passengers extra for carry-on baggage. The CEOs' arguments were pathetic. Well, just as unjustifiable was the "explanation" for trying to charge $215 for grooming a medium-sized dog. The basic price was $80 for "just trimming the ends," and they wanted to add an extra $95 for "full grooming." This is unacceptable; there's nothing that reasonably justifies that exorbitant price of $175 for grooming a medium-sized dog. Some supposed differences in "techniques" were used to justify this irrational price. It's simple... grooming is grooming. When you take your dog to All Grooming, that's what it's for... trimming their fur. Everything else is an unacceptable tactic to inflate prices beyond reason. But the worst part is the staff's complete lack of consideration or intention to correct this exorbitant way of trying to charge such a high price.

This is the last time we will take our dog to this place.

P.S. I read almost all of the responses they give to other customers' terrible experiences, and they're certainly more of the same, so please don't bother replying to this comment. There's no reasonable explanation for what they tried to charge.
